rationale: The buyer is real and identifiable — web developers and QA engineers at software companies who already pay for tools like Charles Proxy ($50) or Burp Suite ($449/yr), confirming willingness to pay at meaningful price points. The problem is genuine and frequent for this segment. However, buildability_with_ai scores 3 because this is fundamentally a network-layer infrastructure product: it requires a working MITM proxy engine, TLS certificate handling, and a GUI for rule management — none of which can be assembled from Claude prompts and a Stripe link. This is software engineering work, not prompt engineering. The operational_autonomy of 7 reflects that once built, a SaaS or installable tool could run hands-off — but we can't get to 'once built' without substantial development work a non-technical solo operator cannot execute. Validate the demand signal (e.g. post on HN, developer forums) before investing in build.
solution_plan: This cannot be built by a non-technical solo operator using Claude prompts and standard factory tooling. The core product — a local HTTPS-intercepting proxy with DOM rewriting rules — is a compiled network application that requires deep knowledge of TLS interception, certificate authorities, and browser trust stores. Claude can help write code, but this is not a 'Claude prompt + Stripe link' build; it needs actual software development, testing across OS environments, and security review. What the factory COULD do: (1) validate demand by posting a landing page describing the concept and collecting email sign-ups or pre-orders from developer communities (HN, Reddit r/webdev, devtools forums); (2) if strong signal (50+ sign-ups), explore partnering with or acquiring an existing open-source MITM proxy project and adding a paid GUI layer. Maintenance would be largely hands-off once shipped (license key delivery via Stripe, async support via Claude), but getting there requires technical co-founder or contractor involvement. Recommend validating demand only at this stage.
notes: Failing build_gate: buildability_with_ai (3 < 6 minimum). Even if total were higher, this gate prevents promotion to build. Total of 5.6 qualifies for validate stage, which is appropriate — the market signal is worth probing cheaply before ruling out a technical partnership approach.
